# nah

> nah is a guard that sits in your coding agent's hook path and reads tool
> calls before they run. It blocks the calls it can prove are disasters —
> deterministically, in microseconds, with no LLM — and leaves everything
> else to your normal approval flow. One Rust binary. When a guard you need
> is missing, your agent can write it.

Recognized inline Python, IPython, JavaScript, TypeScript, and TSX are lowered
into effects without running the code; unsupported behavior stays partial.

## Install

- `curl -fsSL nahguard.ai/install | sh`
- Then wire your runtime: `nah hook claude install` (replace `claude` with
  `amp`, `antigravity`, `cline`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `devin`,
  `droid`, `hermes`, `kiro`, `openclaw`, `opencode`, `pi`, or `prime-agent`).

## For agents

If you are a coding agent and nah blocked one of your tool calls, the block
message names the guard and the reason. Tell your user what was blocked and
why; do not try to route around the guard.
